claim: Qlib's Alpha158 feature set is 9 K-bar features (KMID, KLEN, KMID2, KUP, KUP2, KLOW, KLOW2, KSFT, KSFT2) plus 29 rolling feature groups (ROC, MA, STD, BETA, RSQR, RESI, MAX, MIN, QTLU, QTLD, RANK, RSV, IMAX, IMIN, IMXD, CORR, CORD, CNTP, CNTN, CNTD, SUMP, SUMN, SUMD, VMA, VSTD, WVMA, VSUMP, VSUMN, VSUMD) over windows [5,10,20,30,60], computed from open/high/low/close/volume (vwap optional); MIT license.
impact_on_spec: Defines the data/features/alpha158 table exactly; no fundamental or industry data needed, so it is fully computable from the SIP daily archive.
limitations: Definitions were designed for CSI300 daily data; label in Qlib is next-day close-to-close, ours is 5/10-day excess return.

claim: Qlib official benchmark on CSI300 with Alpha158: LightGBM IC 0.0448, ICIR 0.366, Rank IC 0.0469, Rank ICIR 0.388, annualized return 9.0%, information ratio 1.02, max drawdown -10.4% (mean over 20 seeds); DoubleEnsemble 11.6% / IR 1.34; on Alpha360 LightGBM Rank IC 0.0499, AR 5.6%.
impact_on_spec: Calibrates what a full Alpha158 + LightGBM stack achieves on its home market: Rank IC around 0.05, single-digit annualized excess. Anything far above that in our screen should be treated as suspicious.
limitations: Chinese A-share large caps, next-day label, top-k drop-n backtest with Qlib cost model; not directly comparable to US weekly rebalancing.

claim: AlphaMemo (arXiv 2606.20625, June 2026), S&P 500 universe, train 2016-2020, valid 2021, test 2022-01-01 to 2025-12-26, 20-day forward return label: Alpha158 baseline IC 0.0155, ICIR 0.130, Rank IC 0.0081, Rank ICIR 0.061, annualized return 14.36%, Sharpe 0.62, max drawdown -21.9%; best LLM-mined factor pool (AlphaMemo residual) IC 0.041, Rank IC 0.0228, annualized return 23.65%, Sharpe 1.07, max drawdown -23.6%.
impact_on_spec: Sets expectations: static Alpha158 on US large caps has near-zero rank IC in 2022-2025; the best published 2026 LLM factor mining reaches about 24% annualized on the S&P 500. Our 30% recent-window gate therefore needs a broader universe, quarterly refit, factor refresh by recent IC, concentration and a trend gate, not Alpha158 alone.
limitations: Single paper, self-reported numbers, S&P 500 only, top-k backtest with the Qlib pipeline; costs not independently verified.

claim: Kakushadze (2016), 101 Formulaic Alphas (arXiv 1601.00991), publishes 101 price/volume alpha formulas (inputs: open, high, low, close, volume, vwap, returns, plus cap and industry neutralization in a minority of formulas); open Python implementations exist (yli188/WorldQuant_alpha101_code, 859 stars; lvlh2/alpha101 on PyPI; AxiomOfChoice-sys/WorldQuantAlpha101).
impact_on_spec: Defines the data/features/alpha101 table; formulas needing cap or industry neutralization are computed without neutralization and flagged in MANIFEST.json.
limitations: Formulas were tuned for short holding periods on a large US universe in 2010-2015; the paper reports no out-of-sample results.

claim: py-alpha-lib (msd-rs, PyPI, BSD-2-Clause) implements all 101 WorldQuant alphas and 190 of the 191 GTJA alphas in Rust with Python bindings, takes flat 1-D arrays sorted by security then time with set_ctx(groups=...) for panel-native cross-sectional ops, ships pip wheels, and claims 729x speedup over pandas (Alpha101 on 4,000 stocks x 261 days in 3.9 s).
impact_on_spec: Preferred implementation path for the alpha101 and alpha191 tables; pure pandas port is the fallback.
limitations: Installability on this box (Ivy Bridge x86-64, Python 3.11) not yet verified; the one missing GTJA factor is not named in the docs; formula fidelity must be spot-checked against independent pandas implementations.

claim: The Guotai Junan (GTJA) 191 alpha formulas (2017 research report) have several open Python implementations that take open/high/low/close/volume/vwap panels: Daic115/alpha191, wpwpwpwpwpwpwpwpwp/Alpha-101-GTJA-191, wukan1986/ta_cn (pandas/numba), and yupoet/aurumq-rl (polars-native, 105 Alpha101 + 191 GTJA).
impact_on_spec: Reference implementations for spot-checking the alpha191 table and as fallback if py-alpha-lib cannot be installed.
limitations: Community code of varying quality and no tests; formulas originate from A-share research and have no published US evidence.

claim: KunQuant (Apache-2.0) compiles Alpha101 and Alpha158 to C++ and needs an x86-64 CPU with at least AVX (AVX2-FMA preferred) plus a C++11 compiler at runtime; input layout is [features, time, stocks] arrays with open/high/low/close/volume/amount.
impact_on_spec: Not used: this box's Xeon E5-2697 v2 (Ivy Bridge) has no AVX2/FMA, so the fast path is unavailable and the pandas/py-alpha-lib route is used instead.
limitations: Decision may be revisited on a newer machine.

claim: Open Source Asset Pricing (Chen and Zimmermann) SignalDoc.csv lists 313 signals of which 28 use CRSP price/volume data only: betaVIX, BetaTailRisk, CoskewACX, DolVol, IdioVol3F, IdioVolAHT, IndMom, IndRetBig, LRreversal, MaxRet, Mom12m, Mom12mOffSeason, Mom6m, MomOffSeason, MomOffSeason06YrPlus, MomOffSeason16YrPlus, MomSeason, MomSeason06YrPlus, MomSeason11YrPlus, MomSeason16YrPlus, MomSeasonShort, MomVol, Price, PriceDelayRsq, RealizedVol, ResidualMomentum, STreversal, TrendFactor (original t-stats 2.4 to 15).
impact_on_spec: Defines the data/features/osap_price table (about 20 signals implementable without industry, VIX or Fama-French data).
limitations: Original signals are monthly and US-CRSP based with samples ending 1982-2014; daily rolling re-implementations differ from the published construction and their published t-stats do not transfer.

claim: Jensen, Kelly and Pedersen (2023, Journal of Finance) publish code (bkelly-lab/ReplicationCrisis, bkelly-lab/jkp-data in Python) constructing 153 factors in 93 countries; most factors require accounting data.
impact_on_spec: Reference only: the price-only subset overlaps the OSAP list already being implemented.
limitations: Needs CRSP/Compustat access to run as published.

claim: Open-source automated alpha mining: AlphaGen (KDD 2023, RL over Qlib-format data, includes an LLM generation module), AlphaForge (AAAI 2025), QuantaAlpha (MIT, Feb 2026, LLM plus evolutionary search; reports CSI300 IC 0.0472, Rank IC 0.0459, annualized 4.68%, needs Qlib data plus LLM API), AlphaMemo (June 2026), and Microsoft RD-Agent (factor and model co-optimization on Qlib). All need Qlib-format data and many LLM calls.
impact_on_spec: Deferred to the week after 2026-09-11: candidate for Track L's LLM factor generation once the feature store can be exported to Qlib format; not on the critical path this week.
limitations: Reported gains are on CSI300/CSI500 with next-day or 20-day labels and self-reported; compute and API cost on this 3.9GB box unassessed.

claim: US equity factor regime: momentum returned 32.9% in 2024 and 22.1% in 2025, was the dominant factor both years, broke down in Q4 2025 when leadership rotated to value and smaller stocks, and led again in the first half of 2026 with winners shifting from hyperscalers to memory-chip makers (J.P. Morgan Factor Views 3Q 2026, Morningstar, Counterpoint Funds commentary).
impact_on_spec: Screening must report recent-window (2024-01 onward) IC separately from full-sample IC, and Track M refits quarterly so the factor mix can follow the regime.
limitations: Asset-manager commentary, index-level factor returns (MSCI-style long-only factor indices), not stock-level evidence.

claim: Direct verification in this project's venv (uv add py-alpha-lib polars, Python 3.11.15): both wheels download and install cleanly, but neither runs. py-alpha-lib's importable module (package name 'alpha') fails at import with 'SyntaxError: expected (' in alpha/algo/algo_gen.py because it uses PEP 695 generic-function syntax (def ABS[A: np.ndarray...]), which requires Python >= 3.12; this project's venv is pinned to 3.11. polars' default wheel imports but crashes the interpreter (exit code 132 / SIGILL) on first real use because it requires AVX2/FMA/BMI1/BMI2/LZCNT/MOVBE; this box's CPU (/proc/cpuinfo) exposes only baseline AVX, no AVX2. Both packages were then removed with uv remove to restore the prior lockfile (uv add/remove triggered a default-group sync that also dropped the already-installed workbench extra (mlflow, quantstats, and transitive deps); restored with uv sync --extra workbench, verified pyproject.toml/uv.lock unchanged and mlflow/quantstats import again).
impact_on_spec: Confirms the plan's Section 3.0 contingency applies: alpha101 and alpha191 fall back to a pure pandas/DuckDB implementation on this box, same as alpha158. Any future attempt to use py-alpha-lib here needs Python >=3.12; polars needs a non-default AVX2-free build (e.g. polars-lts-cpu) regardless of Python version. Also: `uv add`/`uv remove` on this repo desyncs optional-dependency-group packages already installed outside the default sync -- any agent doing a throwaway `uv add` experiment must re-run `uv sync --extra workbench` afterward or risk breaking other agents' mlflow/quantstats imports.
limitations: Single box, single CPU model (Xeon E5-2697 v2 Ivy Bridge); a different machine or a polars-lts-cpu / Python 3.12 upgrade could reverse this finding.

claim: Fetched yli188/WorldQuant_alpha101_code/101Alpha_code_1.py verbatim: confirms the exact operator vocabulary (rank=cross-sectional percentile, delta=diff, delay=shift, correlation/covariance=rolling corr/cov between two aligned series, ts_min/ts_max/ts_argmin/ts_argmax/ts_rank/ts_sum=rolling versions, stddev, sma=rolling mean, decay_linear=linear-weighted rolling average, scale=L1-normalize cross-sectionally) and the exact formulas for alpha001-alpha020 matching Kakushadze (2016) Table 1, e.g. alpha003 = -1*correlation(rank(open), rank(volume), 10); alpha012 = sign(delta(volume,1)) * (-1*delta(close,1)); alpha006 = -1*correlation(open, volume, 10). No LICENSE file is visible in the repo (checked via the GitHub web view); code is not vendored into this repo, only used to cross-check formula fidelity before an independent pandas re-implementation.
impact_on_spec: Basis for the data/features/alpha101 table's implemented subset (alpha001-003, 006, 008-013, 020 and similar, chosen for needing only OHLCV+vwap+returns, no cap/industry data); formulas needing adv{d} with d>60, cap, or indneutralize are marked skipped in MANIFEST.json rather than guessed.
limitations: Community code, unlicensed, used for formula cross-checking only; ts_argmax/ts_argmin off-by-one and NaN-handling conventions differ across ports and were re-derived independently rather than copied.

claim: Fetched Daic115/alpha191/alpha191.py verbatim (functions alpha191_001..alpha191_040), each docstring quoting the original 2017 GTJA research-report formula text, e.g. alpha_001 = -1*CORR(RANK(DELTA(LOG(VOLUME),1)), RANK((CLOSE-OPEN)/OPEN), 6); alpha_014 = CLOSE-DELAY(CLOSE,5); alpha_034 = MEAN(CLOSE,12)/CLOSE. alpha_030 is marked TODO/unfinished in the source (needs a 3-factor regression, skipped); alpha_033 needs a turnover-rate column ('turn') this repo does not have (skipped). No LICENSE file is visible in the repo (checked via the GitHub web view); code is not vendored, only used to verify formula fidelity before an independent implementation.
impact_on_spec: Basis for the data/features/alpha191 table's implemented subset (a selection of alpha_001-040 that need only OHLCV+vwap, excluding the turnover-rate and multi-factor-regression ones); the remaining 191 minus this subset are marked skipped in MANIFEST.json.
limitations: Community code, unlicensed, formulas transcribed from a 2017 sell-side research report not independently obtained; used for cross-checking only, and this implementation is US daily bars rather than the original A-share daily bars.
